content.value_statement: Blazor components can behave differently during static SSR, prerendering, and interactive render modes. This skill explains how to use RendererInfo to choose clear UI states and renderer-specific behavior.
actual_capabilities: Explains the purpose of the Blazor RendererInfo class.
Shows how RendererInfo.IsInteractive identifies interactive rendering state.
Lists common RendererInfo.Name values for Static, Server, WebAssembly, and WebView.
Demonstrates disabling UI controls during prerendering.
Compares static SSR content with richer interactive component rendering.
Mentions AssignedRenderMode and the .NET 8 availability requirement.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not inspect or modify a project.
It focuses on RendererInfo and does not cover full Blazor render mode setup.
It applies to .NET 8 and later because RendererInfo is not available earlier.
It does not validate accessibility, security, or performance of generated component designs.

use_cases.title: Guard prerendered controls
use_cases.description: Use RendererInfo.IsInteractive to keep controls disabled until event handlers can run.

use_cases.title: Choose render-specific content
use_cases.description: Show static forms during SSR and switch to richer components after interactive rendering starts.

use_cases.title: Explain render mode behavior
use_cases.description: Document how Static, Server, WebAssembly, and WebView renderer names affect component behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Identify interactive state
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner guidance for a single component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how I can use RendererInfo.IsInteractive in a Blazor component to avoid enabling a button before interactivity starts.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt static and interactive UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Blazor component that shows simple static SSR content first and richer interactive content after RendererInfo reports interactivity.

prompt_templates.title: Compare renderer names
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the RendererInfo.Name values Static, Server, WebAssembly, and WebView, and explain when each should change component behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review a render mode strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for a Blazor app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my plan for using RendererInfo and AssignedRenderMode across a .NET 8 Blazor app, and identify gaps in prerendering behavior.

output_examples.input: Explain when to disable a submit button during Blazor prerendering.
output_examples.output: The response explains that event handlers are inactive during static prerendering, so the button should stay disabled until RendererInfo.IsInteractive is true.

output_examples.input: Help me decide what to show during static SSR versus interactive rendering.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a simple server-rendered form for static SSR and a richer search component after the interactive runtime starts.
The response describes Static, Server, WebAssembly, and WebView as renderer contexts that can guide mode-specific UI decisions.

best_practices: Check RendererInfo.IsInteractive before enabling controls that depend on event handlers.
Use RendererInfo.Name for clear mode-specific branches, not for broad application configuration.
Pair RendererInfo with AssignedRenderMode when you need both current context and assigned mode details.
anti_patterns: Do not assume prerendered buttons can handle events before interactivity starts.
Do not treat RendererInfo.Name as a substitute for configuring render modes correctly.
Do not use this guidance for projects that target versions earlier than .NET 8.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps explain how Blazor RendererInfo can detect interactive state and renderer context inside components.

faq.question: Does it generate full Blazor applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused guidance and examples for RendererInfo usage in Razor components.

faq.question: Which .NET version is required?
faq.answer: RendererInfo is available in .NET 8 and later.

faq.question: Can it help with static SSR?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to adjust UI while a component is prerendered or statically rendered.

faq.question: Does it explain renderer names?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes Static, Server, WebAssembly, and WebView renderer contexts.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
